correctness.rationale: Exact interval-projection identity follows directly from Definition 1.1 with c_n=ω_n/(2κ_(n−1)); overlap iff translation vector is in D=K−K. At contact strict convexity yields precisely two antipodal equality normals. A C² support expansion has Hessian Q=∇²_S h_D+h_D I positive definite, so the excess cap scale is √ε. The cap integral ∫_(|z|≤√2)(1−|z|²/2)dz equals 2^((n+1)/2)κ_(n−1)/(n+1); multiplying both caps and the Kubota prefactor yields 2^((n+3)/2)γ^((n+1)/2)√κ_G/(n+1). The sphere Jacobian tends to one; positive-definite Q gives a uniform O(√ε) support bound and dominated-convergence control. Exact circle and 3D-ball formulas and noncircular ellipses independently check the coefficient; numerical tests are not used to establish the general theorem.

value.rationale: The first-intrinsic-volume metric is a motivated published invariant. Its behavior at disjointness transition was only bounded qualitatively by δ1≤ρ1. The exact critical exponent and constant show how the metric detects the Gauss curvature of K−K from infinitesimally separated translates, in any dimension and any direction, including a nontrivial incidence-angle factor. This is a structural, positive-limit theorem (not a routine restatement of the overlap equality) and provides precise geometric tomography of the difference body.
